{{Short description|Set of axioms for set theory}}
In mathematics, the '''elementary theory of the category of sets''' or '''ETCS''' is a set of [[axiom]]s for [[set theory]] proposed by [[William Lawvere]] in 1964.<ref>William Lawvere, An elementary theory of the category of sets, Proceedings of the National Academy of Science of the U.S.A 52 pp.1506-1511 (1964).</ref> Although it was originally stated in the language of [[category theory]], as [[Tom Leinster]] pointed out, the axioms can be stated without references to category theory.

ETCS is a basic example of [[structural set theory]], an approach to set theory that emphasizes sets as abstract structures (as opposed to collections of elements).

== Axioms ==
{{quote box
|align =right
|width =33%
|quote = The real message is this: simply by writing down a few mundane, uncontroversial statements about sets and functions, we arrive at an axiomatization that reflects how sets are used in everyday mathematics.
|author = Tom Leinster
|source = <ref>{{harvnb|Leinster|2014|loc=The end of the paper.}}</ref>
}}
Informally, the axioms are as follows: (here, set, function and composition of functions are primitives)<ref>{{harvnb|Leinster|2014|loc=Figure 1.}}</ref>
# Composition of functions is associative and has identities.
# There is a set with exactly one element.
# There is an empty set.
# A function is determined by its effect on elements.
# A Cartesian product exists for a pair of sets.
# Given sets <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math>, there is a set of all functions from <math>X</math> to <math>Y</math>.
# Given <math>f : X \to Y</math> and an element <math>y \in Y</math>, the pre-image <math>f^{-1}(y)</math> is defined.
# The subsets of a set <math>X</math> correspond to the functions <math>X \to \{0, 1\}</math>.
# The natural numbers form a set.
# (weak [[axiom of choice]]) Every surjection has a right inverse (i.e., a section).

The resulting theory is weaker than [[ZFC]]. If the [[axiom schema of replacement]] is added as another axiom, the resulting theory is equivalent to ZFC.{{sfn|Leinster|2014|p=412}}
